entries.27c1c832da514dbc: It sells products in 7 categories (Health & Beauty, Paper Products, Pet, Household, Home Care, Household Goods and Others) to retailers nationwide. The company explains that, keeping the “tento” (in-store) perspective in mind and making use of its distinctive information analysis, it has implemented category strategies that capture changes in consumers’ lifestyles and purchasing attitudes. The company has also strengthened its product procurement, planning and development functions and increased exclusive and priority-distribution products, expanding the handling of distinctive products. The company also runs the “Store Management and Field Support Business,” in which advertising jointly planned with manufacturers is proposed to customers, and Instore Marketing Co., Ltd. manages the in-store operations so that the advertising is linked with the customers’ stores.

entries.3f09e689ee881786: [[term:net-income-attributable-to-owners-of-parent|Net income attributable to owners of the parent]] for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥10,130 million (down 2.2% year on year), below the previous year. The company explains that the main factors were cost increases, such as higher logistics and personnel costs due to inflation. The main working capital requirement is purchases of merchandise. Short-term working capital is basically funded by internal funds, short-term borrowings from financial institutions and receivables securitization, while capital expenditure and long-term working capital are basically funded by long-term borrowings from financial institutions and the issuance of bonds.

entries.69e8c9e2ce97efb0: The company’s management vision is “Creating beauty and health, and a clean and comfortable life.” The Medium-Term Management Plan 2026, with the fiscal year ended March 2026 as its final year, achieved net sales of ¥1 trillion, but left challenges in cost control and capital profitability; the company therefore formulated the final-phase Medium-Term Management Plan 2030. Its theme is “Refining strength, opening the future.” It positions the first half as a “strategic investment phase,” as it expects cost increases from growth investments to affect profit, and it aims to improve profitability toward the second half by strengthening the wholesale business and through growth strategies. Business strategies include expanding in-store share through strengthened distinctiveness, establishing new growth drivers, strengthening functions that support sales growth, and improving the profitability of group companies. It sets quantitative targets, including net sales for the fiscal year ending March 2030.

entries.b900fcafab080f5b: A wholesale business that procures products such as daily necessities, cosmetics, household goods and pet supplies and sells them to retailers such as drugstores, home improvement centers, supermarkets and general merchandise stores. ARATA CORPORATION Group treats this as its main business, and as of March 31, 2026 it consists of the Company, 16 consolidated subsidiaries and 2 equity-method affiliates. Because its segment is the single segment of wholesale of daily necessities, cosmetics and related goods, the breakdown of the business is shown by sales results by category. By type of outlet, drugstores are the largest at ¥522,924 million (up 2.3% year on year). In addition, pet supplies are handled by Japell Co., Ltd., a pet specialty wholesaler, and the management of sales floors and support for creating sales floors are carried out by Instore Marketing Co., Ltd. Consolidated net sales for the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥1,004,749 million (up 1.9% year on year), and profit attributable to owners of parent was ¥10,130 million (down 2.2% year on year).

entries.fb3fb675bb5e7a5e: The company describes as its distinctive features its awareness of the “tento” (in-store) perspective since its founding, and its category strategy that captures changes in consumers’ lifestyles and purchasing attitudes by making use of its distinctive information analysis. For pet-related products, it makes proposals that draw on the expertise of Japel Co., Ltd., a pet-specialist wholesale trading company, and says it is strengthening the group’s distinctiveness by expanding exclusive and priority-distribution products.
entries.ff60fd469de935e0: Revenue consists of sales from wholesale of products to retailers. Consolidated revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,004,749 million (up 1.9% year on year), setting a record high for the 11th consecutive period and achieving ¥1 trillion, the target it had set through the fiscal year ended March 2030. The company cites growth in health and beauty and pet products, expanded sales of exclusive and priority-distribution products, and an increase in average unit prices from expanding large-capacity and high-value-added products as factors behind the increase. On the other hand, due to changes in consumer trends, sales volume did not grow, and it did not reach the target of ¥1.006 trillion.
